name: Roledependentnames Pattern
description: Diagram | Intent: | An ontology design pattern for modeling Names as part of Roles, to capture scenarios where an Agent performs different Roles using different Names associated with the different Roles. Examples of an Agent performing a Role using different Names are rather ubiq- uitous, e.g., authors...
competency_questions: Under which name does someone act when they take on a particular role, such as the name an author publishes under?; Given a name, who is behind it and which role were they acting in under that name?; Who or what makes a given role available, and under which names is that role held?
competency_questions_source: derived from the pattern's own axioms during the OntoBoard 1.127.0 review and checked against them; the upstream submission states none
curated: header: dcterms:title "Roledependentnames Pattern" - the library's name for the pattern
header: dcterms:description - the library's description of the pattern

axiom removed: SubObjectPropertyOf(ObjectPropertyChain(<https://kastle-labl.org/lod/ontology/hasName> ObjectInverseOf(<https://kastle-labl.org/lod/ontology/hasRoleUnderName>)) <https://kastle-labl.org/lod/ontology/assumesAgentRole>) - with the chain assumesAgentRole o hasRoleUnderName -> hasName it made a cycle of property chains, outside OWL 2 DL (no reasoner could answer); broken at the inverse that closes it - an agent who acts in a role still carries the role's name

axiom removed: SubClassOf(<https://kastle-labl.org/lod/ontology/Agent> ObjectMaxCardinality(1 ObjectInverseOf(<https://kastle-labl.org/lod/ontology/hasName>) <https://kastle-labl.org/lod/ontology/Name>)) - the chain assumesAgentRole o hasRoleUnderName -> hasName makes hasName a non-simple property, and OWL 2 DL allows no cardinality restriction on one, so no reasoner could answer; this one - on the inverse of hasName - goes, the chain stays (keeping this and dropping that chain instead leaves assumesAgentRole in two cardinality restrictions)
